title: Domestic revenue mobilization is becoming a test of fiscal fairness, administrative capability, and public trust as aid and debt conditions tighten
source_unit: World Bank, Raising Revenue Right: A Roadmap for Domestic Resource Mobilization, 2026
geography: Emerging markets and developing economies, with cross-country fiscal-system comparisons and country-specific reform pathways

observations.period: 2026 report; fiscal conditions in emerging markets and developing economies

fiscal_pressure.value: rising debt burdens, higher interest costs, and less certain external assistance are increasing the need for domestic revenue

revenue_stagnation.value: tax revenues as a share of GDP have remained broadly unchanged while fiscal pressures intensify

system_quality.value: many tax systems combine inefficiency, narrow bases, exemptions or loopholes, and unequal incidence

observations.method: World Bank policy research report synthesizing cross-country fiscal evidence, tax-system analysis, reform research, and country-comparator frameworks for domestic resource mobilization.
observations.uncertainty: The report provides a framework and comparative diagnosis rather than a single causal estimate; tax incidence, administrative quality, informality, and political feasibility differ across countries.
observations.subgroup: Governments, taxpayers, firms, public-service users, vulnerable households, informal workers, and communities affected by tax-and-transfer choices in EMDEs.
observations.counterinterpretation: Weak revenue performance may reflect structural constraints, conflict, informality, commodity cycles, or deliberate policy choices; increasing revenue is not automatically equitable or growth-enhancing.

frontier_definition.value: the best attainable combination of efficiency and fairness for a given level of revenue and structural constraints

tradeoff_diagnosis.value: many countries operate below the fiscal frontier and may improve efficiency, equity, and revenue performance together

reform_principle.value: simplifying rules and reducing poorly targeted exemptions can improve both efficiency and fairness while raising the same amount of revenue

observations.method: Comparative frontier framework that evaluates tax-system performance relative to structural fundamentals and peer economies rather than using a single tax-to-GDP target.
observations.uncertainty: Frontier positions depend on model specification, peer selection, measures of fairness and efficiency, data quality, and assumptions about structural constraints; proximity to a frontier does not prove reform causality.
observations.subgroup: Countries with different institutional, economic, demographic, administrative, and political conditions; taxpayers receiving different public-service and transfer returns from revenue systems.
observations.counterinterpretation: Efficiency gains can still impose distributional costs if transfers, exemptions, enforcement, or public-service allocation do not protect vulnerable households.

observations.period: 2026 report; technology, transparency, and trust route

technology.value: digital systems, information, analytics, and electronic tools can strengthen tax administration and enforcement

transparency.value: transparency and international cooperation can limit avoidance and evasion and clarify who pays and benefits

trust.value: trust in government and tax administration can strengthen voluntary compliance

three_t_link.value: technology, transparency, and trust together expand what tax systems can achieve

observations.method: Policy framework connecting administrative technology, public transparency, international information exchange, taxpayer trust, and voluntary compliance.
observations.uncertainty: The 3T route is a policy theory supported by comparative evidence and research synthesis, not a common experimental estimate of the independent effect of each component.
observations.subgroup: Tax administrations, firms, individuals, public officials, data-system operators, civil society, and people whose willingness to comply depends on perceived fairness and public return.
observations.counterinterpretation: Digitization can widen surveillance, exclusion, or error if identity, appeals, privacy, connectivity, and administrative remedy are weak; transparency can reveal inequity without correcting it.

denominator.unit: broad reform pathways in the World Bank roadmap

build_foundations.value: weaker fundamentals and distance from the frontier call for core administration, registration, filing, simpler compliance, and basic digital systems

expand_coverage.value: countries with weaker fundamentals but nearer the frontier should broaden the tax base and invest in information, property, and taxpayer coverage

simplify_build_trust.value: countries with stronger fundamentals but weaker frontier performance should simplify rules, reduce ineffective exemptions, strengthen enforcement, and improve transparency

deepen_coordination.value: stronger performers can deepen international tax cooperation, beneficial-ownership transparency, data analytics, and contributions from top earners

observations.method: Two-step roadmap: assess structural fundamentals, then compare tax performance with peers sharing similar conditions to identify the relevant reform pathway.
observations.uncertainty: Pathway classification is diagnostic, not a guarantee of implementation or outcome; political coalitions, administrative capacity, taxpayer response, and public-service credibility can alter results.
observations.subgroup: Finance ministries, tax administrations, legislators, firms, households, informal-sector participants, donors, and citizens evaluating the legitimacy of revenue reform.
observations.counterinterpretation: A technically appropriate pathway may fail if it lacks political legitimacy, coordination, protection for low-income households, or credible evidence that new revenue will fund valued public goods.

related_sources.claim: World Bank reproducibility package and report metadata for Raising Revenue Right.
Official report overview, main messages, fiscal-frontier framework, 3T route, and four reform pathways.

boundary: This record adds a domestic-resource-mobilization and public-finance route across fiscal pressure, tax efficiency, equity, administrative technology, transparency, trust, taxpayer compliance, and public-service capacity. It uses a World Bank policy research framework and comparative evidence, not respondent-level ingestion, a complete tax-incidence database, a causal estimate of reform effects, a country-specific implementation evaluation, or proof that more revenue becomes better services or greater legitimacy.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official World Bank report page reviewed for fiscal pressures, stagnant revenue share, fiscal-frontier framework, efficiency-equity claims, technology-transparency-trust route, and four reform pathways; the World Bank reproducibility package reviewed for report metadata and data-access context.
